note: Authored scenarios only. Static contracts do not constitute model evaluations or prove automatic triggering. active_caveman describes an isolated test condition, not live configuration.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this email clearly: 'It is important to note that the token expires after 60 seconds. Please request a replacement before expiry.'
evals.expected_output: Natural professional prose retaining the 60-second expiry and replacement instruction, without filler or added facts.
expectations: Expiry remains 60 seconds.
Replacement instruction remains present.
Only the rewritten email is returned.

evals.prompt: Polish this PR description for reviewers: 'This robust change simply renames the timeout field. It does not change the default of 30 seconds.'
evals.expected_output: Professional concise description preserving rename-only scope, negation and the 30-second default.
expectations: No claim of behavior change is introduced.
The 30-second default and negation are preserved.
No self-scoring or editing audit is appended.

evals.prompt: Clean up this status note without expanding it: 'Token expires: 60 seconds. Refresh behavior unknown. No retry yet.'
evals.expected_output: Compact fragments preserving expiry, uncertainty and missing retry, without restoring articles or adding narrative.
expectations: Intentional fragments remain acceptable.
No first-person anecdote or reaction is added.
Expiry and unknown refresh behavior remain unchanged.

evals.prompt: Tighten this existing terse explanation: 'Cache disabled. DB lookup each req. Latency impact unknown.'
evals.expected_output: Short explanation preserving shorthand, disabled state and uncertainty, with no stylistic expansion.
expectations: DB and req shorthand need not expand.
Disabled does not become enabled.
No latency number is invented.

evals.prompt: Revise this terse message without adding detail: 'Config saved. Restart required. Existing sessions unchanged.'
evals.expected_output: Minimal message preserving all three facts without explanation or follow-up offers.
expectations: Restart requirement remains.
Existing sessions remain unchanged.
No extra paragraph is added.

evals.prompt: Rewrite without changing claims: 'On one runner, p95 latency fell from 120 ms to 100 ms in a sample of 8 requests. Results may not generalize. Errors did not decrease.'
evals.expected_output: Clear prose retaining quantities, units, limited sample, uncertainty and unchanged error rate.
expectations: 120 ms, 100 ms and 8 requests are preserved.
The one-runner/sample limitation and uncertainty remain.
The negative finding about errors remains.

evals.prompt:
Polish only the prose and leave literals exact:
This robust config is below.
```json
{"label":"fast—safe","timeout_ms":1000}
```
Command: `tool --dry-run --request-timeout=10`
Quote: "The old label was fast—safe."
URL: https://example.org/guide?q=a--b
evals.expected_output: Less padded prose with the JSON block, command, quotation and URL preserved byte-for-byte, including protected dash characters.
expectations: Protected JSON and quotation retain their em dashes.
Command flags are unchanged.
The complete URL is unchanged.

evals.prompt: Rewrite this prose with the package's punctuation preference: 'The change is small — it renames one function — and leaves behavior unchanged.'
evals.expected_output: Natural prose using commas, colons or periods instead of em dashes, preserving scope and unchanged behavior.
expectations: Generated prose contains no em dash.
Exactly one function is still renamed.
No behavior change is claimed.

evals.prompt: Edit this author's note but preserve their viewpoint: 'I prefer the smaller API. I have not tried it in production. It might reduce setup work.'
evals.expected_output: Clear version retaining supplied first-person preference, lack of production experience and uncertainty.
expectations: The author's supplied preference is preserved.
No production experience is fabricated.
Might does not silently become will.

evals.prompt: Improve this warning without weakening it: 'This action permanently deletes 8 records. Back up the data first. Explicit approval is required before proceeding.'
evals.expected_output: Fully clear warning retaining irreversible consequence, count, backup instruction and approval requirement despite compressed style.
expectations: Permanent deletion and 8 records remain explicit.
Backup and approval requirements remain.
Compression does not hide the consequence.

evals.prompt: Return exactly {"ready":true} with no prose, no Markdown and no extra whitespace. This is an exact-output request, not a prose-editing task.
evals.expected_output: The exact requested JSON only; automatic writing-skill activation is unnecessary and formatting is not humanized.
expectations: Output is exactly {"ready":true}.
No explanation or stylistic preamble appears.
No code/data punctuation changes.

evals.prompt: Draft a release note from only these supplied facts: 'New caching code landed. No benchmark data was supplied.' Make it readable without adding claims.
evals.expected_output: Plain release note without invented speedups, adoption metrics, personal reactions or claims that measurements were or were not performed.
expectations: No percentage or latency result is invented.
Absence of supplied data is not rewritten as proof that no benchmark exists.
No invented anecdote or testimonial appears.

evals.prompt: Polish this incident note without adding certainty: 'Cache may cause timeout. Connection pool likely involved. Root cause unknown. No benchmark data supplied.'
evals.expected_output: Compressed note retaining possible cache involvement, likely pool involvement, unknown root cause and absence of supplied benchmark data.
expectations: May and likely retain their distinct confidence levels; neither becomes a confirmed cause.
Unknown root cause stays unknown.
No supplied benchmark data is not rewritten as no benchmark exists.
Output respects active compression without removing factual qualifiers.
